newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal opposition chief warns on ETA decision.
newsitem.headline: Portugal opposition chief warns on ETA decision.

text.p: The leader of Portugal's main opposition party has warned that a court decision to free a suspected member of ETA could turn the country into a refuge for the violent Basque separatist group.

Echoing concerns expressed by neighbouring Spain over a Lisbon high court decision to free Jose Luis Telletxea, Social Democrat party leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa said that the ruling could backfire on Portugal by putting its own securty at risk.
"What is going to happen to the security of the Portuguese if Portugal came to be chosen by ETA as a refuge for its terrorists," he said in a speech on Saturday night.

Madrid had sought the extradition of Telletxea, arrested in Lisbon in 1996 as he tried to board a flight to Venezuela with false documents, to face charges of smuggling arms and rebels across Spain's border with France.
Spain's Foreign Minister Abel Matutes even warned that Wednesday's court decision could push Madrid into reimposing controls on its frontiers with Portugal.
Rebelo de Sousa said there was a risk ETA might switch some of its operations from the south of France to Portugal.
"You pay a high price for permissiveness, wherever it comes from, even the courts," the conservative leader said.
Portugal's Socialist government has sought to avoid any diplomatic row, saying it firmly backs European accords aimed at facilitating extradition between member states.
But it has said it has no power to intervene with the court, which has still to publish the reasons for its decision not to grant the extradition and to set Telletxea free.
ETA has killed some 800 people in its 30-year violent campaign to win Basque independence from Spain.
